modules.title: Advanced Window Functions and Frames
modules.goal: Use ranking, frames and distribution functions for serious analytical queries.

topics.title: Ranking vs Row Number
topics.simple: Ranking ties ko same number deta hai; row number unique rehta hai.
topics.pro: RANK shares numbers across ties and leaves gaps, DENSE_RANK shares without gaps, and ROW_NUMBER is unique but arbitrary on ties.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS r, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS d, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC, id) AS rn FROM students;

topics.title: Top N per Group
topics.simple: Partitioned row numbers se har group ka top N nikaalo.
topics.pro: Top-N per group ranks rows inside each partition and filters the rank in an outer query.

example.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT course_id, student_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY student_id) AS rn FROM enrollments) SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;

topics.title: Running Totals
topics.simple: Running total ordered rows ko accumulate karta hai.
topics.pro: A running total uses SUM with an unbounded preceding frame and restarts per partition.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running FROM students;

topics.title: Moving Averages
topics.simple: Moving average window ke andar ke rows ka average deta hai.
topics.pro: A moving average uses a bounded frame and a stable order so each row sees the same number of neighbors.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, AVG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg FROM students;

topics.title: Frame Boundaries
topics.simple: Frame ka start aur end explicitly set karo.
topics.pro: Frame boundaries use UNBOUNDED PRECEDING, n PRECEDING, CURRENT ROW, n FOLLOWING and UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING.
points: The default frame is RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS nearby FROM students;

topics.title: ROWS Frame
topics.simple: ROWS physical row offsets par kaam karta hai.
topics.pro: ROWS counts actual rows, so duplicate ORDER BY values are still separate frame positions.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, AVG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg2 FROM students;

topics.title: RANGE Frame
topics.simple: RANGE ORDER BY values ke ranges par kaam karta hai.
topics.pro: RANGE includes peer rows with equal ORDER BY values, so duplicates move through the frame together.

example.sql: SELECT marks, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY marks RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative FROM students;
example.output: Tied marks receive the same cumulative value.

topics.title: GROUPS Frame
topics.simple: GROUPS peer groups ke offsets par kaam karta hai.
topics.pro: GROUPS counts peer groups rather than physical rows, which is useful when ties should be one unit.
points: It sits between ROWS and RANGE.

example.sql: SELECT marks, AVG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY marks GROUPS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS grouped_avg FROM students;
example.output: Averages over the previous peer group and the current group.

topics.title: EXCLUDE Clause
topics.simple: EXCLUDE current row ya peers ko frame se hataata hai.
topics.pro: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW, EXCLUDE GROUP and EXCLUDE TIES remove rows from the frame for calculations such as leave-one-out averages.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, AVG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW) AS neighbor_avg FROM students;

topics.title: LAG and LEAD
topics.simple: LAG previous aur LEAD next row deta hai.
topics.pro: LAG and LEAD compare a row with an earlier or later row using an offset and optional default.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, marks - LAG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS delta FROM students;
example.output: The change from the previous mark.

topics.title: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE
topics.simple: Frame ke first aur last value dete hain.
topics.pro: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE return boundary values from the frame, so the frame definition determines the result.
points: LAST_VALUE needs a full frame for the last row.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, FIRST_VALUE(name) OVER (PARTITION BY marks ORDER BY id) AS first_peer FROM students;
example.output: The first student at each mark.

topics.title: NTH_VALUE
topics.simple: NTH_VALUE frame ka Nth row deta hai.
topics.pro: NTH_VALUE returns the value at a one-based position inside the frame, with an optional direction.
points: The frame must include the row.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, NTH_VALUE(name, 2) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS second_name FROM students;
example.output: The second-highest name on every row.

topics.title: PERCENT_RANK
topics.simple: PERCENT_RANK relative percentile rank deta hai.
topics.pro: PERCENT_RANK returns (rank - 1) / (rows - 1), giving a value from 0 to 1 for ordered rows.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks) AS pct FROM students;

topics.title: CUME_DIST
topics.simple: CUME_DIST cumulative distribution deta hai.
topics.pro: CUME_DIST returns the fraction of rows at or below the current peer group, always greater than zero and at most one.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY marks) AS cume FROM students;

topics.title: NTILE Buckets
topics.simple: NTILE ordered rows ko equal buckets me baantta hai.
topics.pro: NTILE(n) assigns bucket numbers from 1 to n, with earlier buckets taking the extra rows.
points: Buckets differ by at most one.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS quartile FROM students;

topics.title: Percent of Total
topics.simple: Window sum se row ka percent of total nikaalo.
topics.pro: Dividing a row value by SUM over an empty window produces its share of the total without a separate aggregate query.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks, ROUND(100.0 * marks / SUM(marks) OVER (), 2) AS pct FROM students;
example.output: Each mark as a percentage of the total.

topics.title: Difference from Previous
topics.simple: LAG se previous value ka difference nikaalo.
topics.pro: Subtracting LAG from the current value gives a row-to-row delta, with NULL for the first row.

example.sql: SELECT id, marks, marks - LAG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS delta FROM students;
example.output: The change from the prior row.

topics.title: Median with PERCENTILE_CONT
topics.simple: PERCENTILE_CONT continuous percentile deta hai.
topics.pro: PERCENTILE_CONT interpolates between values to return a continuous percentile, commonly the median at 0.5.
points: It returns one row per group.

example.sql: SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY marks) AS median FROM students;

topics.title: Mode with MODE
topics.simple: MODE sabse frequent value deta hai.
topics.pro: MODE() WITHIN GROUP returns the most frequent input value, and PostgreSQL picks the first one when there is a tie.

example.sql: SELECT MODE() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY marks) AS mode FROM students;

topics.title: Practical Ranking Report
topics.simple: Ranking, percent of total aur top N ko report me combine karo.
topics.pro: A production ranking report uses a CTE for window calculations, filters the rank outside and presents a stable order.

example.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT name, marks, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS r, ROUND(100.0 * marks / SUM(marks) OVER (), 2) AS pct FROM students) SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE r <= 5 ORDER BY r;
example.output: Top five with rank and share.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Ranking vs Row Number in a production query.
interview.answer: RANK shares numbers across ties and leaves gaps, DENSE_RANK shares without gaps, and ROW_NUMBER is unique but arbitrary on ties. Key rules: Choose by tie semantics. ROW_NUMBER needs a total order. DENSE_RANK is compact.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Top N per Group in a production query.
interview.answer: Top-N per group ranks rows inside each partition and filters the rank in an outer query. Key rules: Partition by the group. Order by the ranking key. Filter the rank outside.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Running Totals in a production query.
interview.answer: A running total uses SUM with an unbounded preceding frame and restarts per partition. Key rules: Order by a stable key. Use UNBOUNDED PRECEDING. Partition for group totals.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Moving Averages in a production query.
interview.answer: A moving average uses a bounded frame and a stable order so each row sees the same number of neighbors. Key rules: Pick the frame width. Use ROWS for exact counts. Use RANGE for date windows.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Frame Boundaries in a production query.
interview.answer: Frame boundaries use UNBOUNDED PRECEDING, n PRECEDING, CURRENT ROW, n FOLLOWING and UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING. Key rules: Start must not follow end. The default frame is RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW. Frames require ORDER BY.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain ROWS Frame in a production query.
interview.answer: ROWS counts actual rows, so duplicate ORDER BY values are still separate frame positions. Key rules: Exact row counts. Duplicates are separate. Good for moving averages.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain RANGE Frame in a production query.
interview.answer: RANGE includes peer rows with equal ORDER BY values, so duplicates move through the frame together. Key rules: Peers share a frame. Good for value ranges. Date ranges use intervals.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain GROUPS Frame in a production query.
interview.answer: GROUPS counts peer groups rather than physical rows, which is useful when ties should be one unit. Key rules: Groups are peer sets. It sits between ROWS and RANGE. It needs ORDER BY.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain EXCLUDE Clause in a production query.
interview.answer: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW, EXCLUDE GROUP and EXCLUDE TIES remove rows from the frame for calculations such as leave-one-out averages. Key rules: It applies after the frame. PostgreSQL supports it. It is useful for comparisons.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain LAG and LEAD in a production query.
interview.answer: LAG and LEAD compare a row with an earlier or later row using an offset and optional default. Key rules: Offset defaults to 1. Order must be deterministic. Partition for group-local comparisons.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE in a production query.
interview.answer: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE return boundary values from the frame, so the frame definition determines the result. Key rules: They respect the frame. LAST_VALUE needs a full frame for the last row. Partition for group boundaries.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain NTH_VALUE in a production query.
interview.answer: NTH_VALUE returns the value at a one-based position inside the frame, with an optional direction. Key rules: Position is one-based. The frame must include the row. It returns NULL when absent.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain PERCENT_RANK in a production query.
interview.answer: PERCENT_RANK returns (rank - 1) / (rows - 1), giving a value from 0 to 1 for ordered rows. Key rules: It uses RANK semantics. The best row is 0. The worst row is 1.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain CUME_DIST in a production query.
interview.answer: CUME_DIST returns the fraction of rows at or below the current peer group, always greater than zero and at most one. Key rules: It includes peers. It is cumulative. It differs from PERCENT_RANK.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain NTILE Buckets in a production query.
interview.answer: NTILE(n) assigns bucket numbers from 1 to n, with earlier buckets taking the extra rows. Key rules: It needs an order. Buckets differ by at most one. It is good for quartiles.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Percent of Total in a production query.
interview.answer: Dividing a row value by SUM over an empty window produces its share of the total without a separate aggregate query. Key rules: Use SUM(...) OVER (). Guard against zero. Round at display time.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Difference from Previous in a production query.
interview.answer: Subtracting LAG from the current value gives a row-to-row delta, with NULL for the first row. Key rules: Order by the event key. Handle the first NULL. Partition for restarts.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Median with PERCENTILE_CONT in a production query.
interview.answer: PERCENTILE_CONT interpolates between values to return a continuous percentile, commonly the median at 0.5. Key rules: It uses WITHIN GROUP. It interpolates. It returns one row per group.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Mode with MODE in a production query.
interview.answer: MODE() WITHIN GROUP returns the most frequent input value, and PostgreSQL picks the first one when there is a tie. Key rules: It uses WITHIN GROUP. It ignores NULL. Ties are resolved arbitrarily.

interview.q: Module 16 · Explain Practical Ranking Report in a production query.
interview.answer: A production ranking report uses a CTE for window calculations, filters the rank outside and presents a stable order. Key rules: Calculate windows in a CTE. Filter in the outer query. Order the final report.

labs.task: Write a SQL example that demonstrates Percent of Total.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks, ROUND(100.0 * marks / SUM(marks) OVER (), 2) AS pct FROM students;
labs.expected: Each mark as a percentage of the total.

labs.title: Difference from Previous
labs.task: Write a SQL example that demonstrates Difference from Previous.
labs.solution: SELECT id, marks, marks - LAG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS delta FROM students;
labs.expected: The change from the prior row.

labs.title: Median with PERCENTILE_CONT
labs.task: Write a SQL example that demonstrates Median with PERCENTILE_CONT.
labs.solution: SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY marks) AS median FROM students;

labs.title: Mode with MODE
labs.task: Write a SQL example that demonstrates Mode with MODE.
labs.solution: SELECT MODE() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY marks) AS mode FROM students;

labs.title: Practical Ranking Report
labs.task: Write a SQL example that demonstrates Practical Ranking Report.
labs.solution: WITH ranked AS (SELECT name, marks, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS r, ROUND(100.0 * marks / SUM(marks) OVER (), 2) AS pct FROM students) SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE r <= 5 ORDER BY r;
labs.expected: Top five with rank and share.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does Ranking vs Row Number matter?
logic.answer: RANK shares numbers across ties and leaves gaps, DENSE_RANK shares without gaps, and ROW_NUMBER is unique but arbitrary on ties. Choose by tie semantics. ROW_NUMBER needs a total order. DENSE_RANK is compact.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does Top N per Group matter?
logic.answer: Top-N per group ranks rows inside each partition and filters the rank in an outer query. Partition by the group. Order by the ranking key. Filter the rank outside.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does Running Totals matter?
logic.answer: A running total uses SUM with an unbounded preceding frame and restarts per partition. Order by a stable key. Use UNBOUNDED PRECEDING. Partition for group totals.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does Moving Averages matter?
logic.answer: A moving average uses a bounded frame and a stable order so each row sees the same number of neighbors. Pick the frame width. Use ROWS for exact counts. Use RANGE for date windows.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does Frame Boundaries matter?
logic.answer: Frame boundaries use UNBOUNDED PRECEDING, n PRECEDING, CURRENT ROW, n FOLLOWING and UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING. Start must not follow end. The default frame is RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW. Frames require ORDER BY.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does ROWS Frame matter?
logic.answer: ROWS counts actual rows, so duplicate ORDER BY values are still separate frame positions. Exact row counts. Duplicates are separate. Good for moving averages.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does RANGE Frame matter?
logic.answer: RANGE includes peer rows with equal ORDER BY values, so duplicates move through the frame together. Peers share a frame. Good for value ranges. Date ranges use intervals.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does GROUPS Frame matter?
logic.answer: GROUPS counts peer groups rather than physical rows, which is useful when ties should be one unit. Groups are peer sets. It sits between ROWS and RANGE. It needs ORDER BY.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does EXCLUDE Clause matter?
logic.answer: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW, EXCLUDE GROUP and EXCLUDE TIES remove rows from the frame for calculations such as leave-one-out averages. It applies after the frame. PostgreSQL supports it. It is useful for comparisons.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does LAG and LEAD matter?
logic.answer: LAG and LEAD compare a row with an earlier or later row using an offset and optional default. Offset defaults to 1. Order must be deterministic. Partition for group-local comparisons.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE matter?
logic.answer: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE return boundary values from the frame, so the frame definition determines the result. They respect the frame. LAST_VALUE needs a full frame for the last row. Partition for group boundaries.
NTH_VALUE returns the value at a one-based position inside the frame, with an optional direction. Position is one-based. The frame must include the row. It returns NULL when absent.
PERCENT_RANK returns (rank - 1) / (rows - 1), giving a value from 0 to 1 for ordered rows. It uses RANK semantics. The best row is 0. The worst row is 1.
CUME_DIST returns the fraction of rows at or below the current peer group, always greater than zero and at most one. It includes peers. It is cumulative. It differs from PERCENT_RANK.

logic.q: Module 16 · Why does NTILE Buckets matter?
logic.answer: NTILE(n) assigns bucket numbers from 1 to n, with earlier buckets taking the extra rows. It needs an order. Buckets differ by at most one. It is good for quartiles.

debug.title: Top N filtered too early
debug.broken: SELECT course_id, student_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY student_id) AS rn FROM enrollments WHERE rn <= 3;
debug.fix: WITH ranked AS (SELECT course_id, student_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY student_id) AS rn FROM enrollments) SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3;

debug.title: Default frame surprise
debug.broken: SELECT id, marks, LAST_VALUE(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS last_mark FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT id, marks, LAST_VALUE(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_mark FROM students;
debug.error: LAST_VALUE sees only up to the current row

debug.title: RANGE with integer offsets
debug.broken: SELECT id, marks, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id RANGE BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT id, marks, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM students;
debug.error: RANGE offsets must match the ORDER BY type

debug.title: Missing ORDER BY
debug.broken: SELECT id, SUM(marks) OVER (ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT id, SUM(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM students;

debug.title: PERCENTILE without WITHIN GROUP
debug.broken: SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) OVER (ORDER BY marks) FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY marks) FROM students;

debug.title: MODE as a window
debug.fix: SELECT MODE() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY marks) FROM students;
debug.error: MODE is not a window function

debug.title: NTILE without order
debug.fix: SELECT NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) FROM students;

debug.title: Wrong NTH_VALUE index
debug.broken: SELECT NTH_VALUE(name, 0) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT NTH_VALUE(name, 1) OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) FROM students;
debug.error: NTH_VALUE position must be greater than zero

debug.title: Exclusion syntax
debug.broken: SELECT AVG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING EXCLUDE) FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT AVG(marks) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW) FROM students;

debug.title: Percent divide by zero
debug.broken: SELECT 100 * marks / SUM(marks) OVER () FROM students;
debug.fix: SELECT 100.0 * marks / NULLIF(SUM(marks) OVER (), 0) FROM students;
debug.error: division by zero when the total is zero
